Hi Alex / Priya — following up with the technical notes we discussed. Key points below and a couple of minimal snippets.

Auth / SDK:
- Use Redwood SDK token tied to your service account. For Private deployments we recommend short-lived tokens backed by your KMS and a rotation policy (rotate every 24h). We can provide a Lambda example for rotation if you want.
- SDKs support both HTTP/REST and gRPC. gRPC + persistent connection reduces TLS handshake latency for high-throughput routing.

Chat vs Completions (short):
- Chat is stateful (messages array) and better for multi-turn where role/metadata is important. It also has richer structured tool-calling semantics (function calls).
- Completions are single-prompt -> single-output, slightly cheaper for one-shot generation and simpler token accounting. Good for generation from a merged prompt (e.g., reranked context + template).

Tokenization, max_tokens, stop sequences:
- Tokenization differences: both endpoints use the same tokenizer for a given model; however, chat SDK applies role/message metadata which can change token counts (system tokens, role prefixes). Be conservative with prompt sizing and measure tokens via the SDK token_count helper.
- max_tokens is a hard cap on generated tokens. For streaming, tokens are emitted as generated; if you set a stop sequence, generation halts when a full stop pattern is emitted in the decoded stream.
- Important: stop sequences are matched on decoded text, not token boundaries — so there can be partial tokens buffered and then matched. If you rely on exact JSON close-brace as a stop, prefer explicit function-calling (structured output) or return delimiting markers like "---END---" to be safe.

Streaming semantics example (pseudo):
- Chat streaming: open a stream, send initial messages, then server streams delta events with tokens/partial text and an optional final 'done' event with full output. You can parse and assemble partial JSON, but keep an eye on truncated tokens.
- If you need guaranteed well-formed JSON, either use function-calling (Redwood will return a parsed JSON object) or ask the model to emit JSON wrapped in a code fence and also include an MD5 checksum field so you can validate completeness.

Snippets (high-level):
- Chat streaming: connect -> send messages -> listen for 'token' events -> on 'done' verify stop reason.
- Completions (no streaming): call completions endpoint with prompt + max_tokens + stop -> receive complete text.

I'll attach a short sample showing both; if you want, Marcus and I can pair with your engs for 45m to run the sample against your sandbox.

- Dev

Alex — great questions. Short answers and next actions: 

1) Proxying directly to browser: technically feasible but we recommend server-side proxying for two reasons: avoids leaking model tokens/metadata to the client, and lets you centralize auth/decoding/retries. If low latency is required and you have edge servers, you can establish a persistent gRPC connection from edge -> Redwood and stream to the browser from your edge. We can share a reference architecture.

2) Structured JSON reliability: function-calling is our recommended approach for strict schemas — Redwood will return a validated object (parsed) rather than raw text when a function schema is provided, which avoids truncation/partial JSON issues. It can be slightly more (1.05x–1.2x) in cost vs free-form completions depending on the number of tokens generated, but the reliability win is typically worth it. If you must stream text, add delimiting markers and a checksum as Dev suggested, and validate on completion.

3) Token budget: with 3k tokens of context, start with max_tokens = 512 and reserve a safety margin (e.g., 10–15%) to avoid cut-off, so plan for total tokens (context + max_tokens + system overhead) < model max. Use the SDK token_count helper to measure average prompt tokens after reranking. If you see frequent truncation, either reduce context, increase max_tokens, or switch to retrieval brevity (shorter context + pointers).

Next actions: Marcus can set up a 45-min pairing session this Wed or Thu to run the sample against your sandbox and iterate on function schema. Please confirm availability.
